welcome.title: Welcome to Clickr
body: Windows autoclicker with a native motor (SendInput).
Use the pulse button or the hotkey (default F6) to start and stop.
The window X does not quit the app — it goes to the tray. To quit for real: tray icon → Quit.
tips: Click the F6 keycap in the footer to record another shortcut key.
Want a guided preset? Use Wizard mode at the top of this tab.

click.title: Click tab — essentials
body: Interval (ms) + slider: time between clicks. Estimated CPS appears below.
Button: L / R / M / 4 / 5 (side mouse buttons).
Type: Single, Double, or Hold (keeps pressed until stop).
Position: Cursor (where the mouse is) or Fixed point (XY).
tips: Hold releases the button when you stop the engine.
After the Wizard, change everything again on this tab.

run.title: Run tab — limits and extras
body: Start delay: wait before the first click (useful to return to the target window).
Jitter ±: random variation on the interval (less “mechanical” clicks).
Click limit / max duration: stops alone when N or the time is reached.
Always on top: window above others. Compact mode: hides Adv, Macro, Script, and Schedule.

point.title: Point tab — coordinates
body: Set X and Y manually or use Capture point (overlay on all monitors).
Sequence: list of points with per-step delay. The engine cycles the list when not empty.
+ point uses the current cursor position (or XY if provided).
tips: Esc cancels capture. Click marks the real OS cursor position.

profiles.title: Profiles tab
body: Save the current config with a name under %APPDATA%/Clickr/profiles/.
Load applies a profile from the list. Export/Import swaps JSON with other machines.

advanced.title: Adv tab — filter and burst
body: Window filter: only clicks if the focused process and/or title match.
Burst: N fast clicks, pause, repeat — useful for controlled bursts.
Buttons 4 and 5 are on the Click tab selector.
tips: With filter on and empty criteria, all clicks are allowed.

macro.title: Macro tab
body: Record: captures mouse and keyboard with relative timing.
Play: resends events via SendInput.
Stop / Clear interrupt or erase the recording.
tips: During recording, the engine toggle hotkey is ignored.

script.title: Script tab — DSL
body: Commands: click [button], move X Y, wait ms, key NAME, loop N … end.
Limits: up to 500 lines, loops 1–1000, loop depth ≤ 2.
Run / Stop control the runner.
tips: Example: move 100 200 → click left → wait 100 → key SPACE

schedule.title: Schedule tab
body: Pick a local date/time and Schedule.
When the time arrives, the click engine starts on its own.
Cancel removes the pending schedule.

safety.title: Responsible use
body: Use only where you have authorization.
In online games / anti-cheat, an autoclicker may violate terms and cause a ban.
Clickr does not bypass anti-cheat. Admin windows may ignore input if Clickr is not elevated.
tips: You are responsible for how you use the software.

mouse_buttons.title: Mouse buttons (L R M 4 5)
body: L — left button (the “normal” click).
R — right button (context menu).
M — middle button (usually the wheel pressed).
4 and 5 — side buttons (back/forward), if your mouse has them.

click_type.title: Click type
body: Single — one click at a time, at the interval pace.
Double — two quick clicks each cycle (like double-clicking an icon).
Hold — keeps the button pressed until you stop Clickr (not repeated clicking).

interval.title: Interval and CPS
body: Interval is the pause between one click and the next, in milliseconds (ms). 1000 ms = 1 second.
E.g.: 80 ms ≈ 12.5 clicks per second (CPS).
Smaller numbers = faster. Start slower when testing.

position.title: Where to click
body: Cursor — clicks where the mouse is at the time (you can move while it runs).
Fixed point — always the same screen coordinate (X, Y).
Capture point — the screen dims; click the desired place (Esc cancels). Works on all monitors.

limits.title: What are limits?
body: Optional stops so Clickr does not run forever. You can leave everything empty/zero and adjust later on the Run tab.

delay.title: Start delay
body: Wait time before the first click, after you hit Start.
Useful so you can press Start and still return to the right game or window.
E.g.: 2000 ms = waits 2 seconds, then starts clicking.

jitter.title: Jitter (±)
body: Random variation on the interval so clicks are not 100% robotic.
E.g.: interval 80 ms and jitter 10 → each pause is between ~70 and ~90 ms.
0 = no variation (fixed rhythm).

max_clicks.title: Click limit
body: Maximum number of clicks. When reached, Clickr stops on its own.
Empty field (∞) = no quantity limit.

max_duration.title: Max duration
body: Maximum time the engine stays active, in milliseconds.
E.g.: 10000 = stops automatically after 10 seconds.
Empty field (∞) = no time limit.

profile.title: Profile (preset)
body: A name to store this configuration and reuse later.
Lives on the Profiles tab (load, export, import).
Afterwards you can change button, interval, etc. on Click / Run / Point without redoing the Wizard.
